text: Sunday night, November 22nd, 1987. Chicago, Illinois. Nine p.m. — and the evening news is on.
image: 1980s Chicago living room at night, family silhouettes watching a glowing CRT television showing the evening news, warm lamp glow, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: The sports highlights are wrapping up. Then — the screen goes black.

text: For about twenty-five seconds, something else fills the screen. Something that was never supposed to be there.

text: A figure in a rubber mask — rocking side to side, humming. Silent. Staring straight at you.

text: Honestly, this part still gives me chills — because two hours later, he came back. And this time, he stayed for ninety seconds.

text: To understand what happened that night, you need to know who Max Headroom was.
image: 1980s television set showing a fictional stuttering computer-generated TV host character in a neon studio, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: Max Headroom was the first computer-generated TV personality — a wisecracking, stuttering host from the mid-eighties.
image: Retro 1980s television studio with a digital grid background and a robotic TV host, neon lights, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: He had his own show. He starred in soda commercials. Everybody in America knew that face.
image: 1980s living room with kids laughing at a TV showing a soda commercial with a digital host, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: And that rubber mask? You could buy one in any costume shop for a few dollars.
image: Dusty 1980s costume shop shelf lined with rubber TV-host masks and price tags, dim bulb, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: But on one Sunday night in Chicago, somebody turned that joke into a federal crime.
image: Rubber TV-host mask lying on a dark table next to microwave transmitter equipment under dramatic light, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: And nearly four decades later — nobody has ever been caught.

text: Let’s go back to nine fourteen p.m. WGN, Channel 9 — Chicago’s biggest independent station.

text: The sports anchor is on screen, all smiles, running through the football highlights.

text: For twenty-five seconds, the masked figure is there — rocking, humming, saying nothing at all.

text: Just like that, the news is back. Twenty-five seconds. No audio. Gone.
image: TV screen returning to the news anchor, a family in a living room looking at each other confused, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: Most viewers thought their TV was broken. But the intruder wasn’t done. He was just warming up.
image: Masked figure silhouette in a dark room adjusting a microwave dish antenna with city lights below, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: Because he had found a second target — a station with no backup at all.
image: Small public TV station building at night with a single dim tower on a quiet street, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: Eleven fifteen p.m. WTTW, Channel 11 — Chicago’s public television station.
image: Public TV station sign glowing at night on a modest brick building, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: Doctor Who is on — a calm, nerdy Sunday-night ritual for thousands of viewers.

text: Ninety seconds. And then — the signal dies. The Doctor is back, mid-sentence, like nothing happened.

text: In my opinion, the scariest part isn’t the mask — it’s that someone rehearsed all of this, down to the second, and nobody stopped them.

text: So how do you hijack a TV station in 1987? Honestly — the method was almost elegant.
image: Microwave transmission tower at dusk with visualized signal waves, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: Every station beams its picture from the studio to its transmitter tower by microwave link.
image: Diagram-style illustration of a studio beaming a microwave signal to a tall tower, 1980s technology, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: The hijacker aimed his own, more powerful transmitter at that same tower.
image: Shadowy figure on a rooftop aiming a dish antenna at a distant broadcast tower at night, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: When his signal overpowered the station’s — his video won. Engineers call it an STL override.
image: Two signal waves colliding with the stronger wave swallowing the weaker one, tower silhouette, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: But here’s the catch: microwaves need a clear line of sight. He had to be up high, close by.
image: Chicago skyline at night with a beam of light drawn from a rooftop to a tower, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: That means expensive gear, real know-how — and nerves of steel.
image: 1980s microwave transmitter equipment with dials and gauges, gloved hands adjusting, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark

text: This was no kid with a remote control. This was someone who understood broadcast engineering.
image: Hooded engineer silhouette studying broadcast schematics by flashlight, storybook noir, 2D digital storybook illustration, dark noir documentary style, 16:9, cinematic, no text, no watermark
